extracted.intended_audience: CHI 2010 paper reviewers / subcommittee reviewers / program committee
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewing Papers and Notes submitted to the CHI 2010 conference, including how to use contribution types, subcommittees, numeric ratings, and written appraisals to judge whether a submission makes a strong contribution to HCI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Primary contribution criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Does this submission provide a strong contribution to the field of HCI?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is your primary criterion for judging a paper. Evaluate the submission primarily on whether it makes a strong contribution to HCI rather than on peripheral factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution-type-specific evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the questions about contributions as specified in the description of each contribution type; authors indicate a contribution type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contribution-type description includes a set of questions you should consider when evaluating contribution. These questions may push you to think about contribution in ways that differ from the typical CHI 'formula' — use them as a guide. They are not a checklist; a submission may not cleanly fall within a single type and should not be penalized for that. If the paper makes a contribution outside the specified questions, judge it accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contribution Type Specific Rating (form field)
rubrics_metrics.description: A contribution-type specific rating appears on the review form; by filling it in you judge the paper according to its declared contribution type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the contribution type as a starting point when appraising the contribution, but the paper need not exactly match the contribution type criteria. Do not require an exact fit between paper and contribution-type questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Rating (form field)
rubrics_metrics.description: An Overall Rating appears immediately after the contribution-type rating; by filling it in you judge the overall contribution of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use your overall judgement of the paper's contribution to HCI when completing this rating. The contribution-type rating can inform but should not rigidly determine the overall rating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not judge by subcommittee fit
rubrics_metrics.description: You should not judge a paper by how well it fits the subcommittee theme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcommittees exist to improve reviewer matching, but matches are not always clean. Many papers will not fit neatly into a single subcommittee; evaluate such papers on their merits. Any topic is valid as long as it fits within the interests of a reasonable fraction of the overall CHI audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers versus Notes: appropriate expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers and Notes are reviewed within the same rigorous review process and at the highest level judged by similar criteria (does it provide a strong contribution?), but the type of content appropriate for each is different.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes present brief and focused research contributions that are noteworthy but may not be as complete or provide the same depth of results as a full paper. Apply expectations about scope and completeness accordingly when judging Papers vs Notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numeric rating scale and accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Numeric ratings use a 5-point scale (with half steps) from 1.0 (lowest) to 5.0 (highest).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be as accurate as possible when assigning numeric ratings. Use half steps where appropriate to reflect nuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written appraisal must support numeric rating
rubrics_metrics.description: Your written appraisal must support your numeric ranking and indicate why the paper deserves that rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure details in the written review reflect the numeric rating. A review may be discounted if, for example, you numerically rate a paper highly but only indicate its flaws. Make sure to explain the reasons behind the score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balanced, polite, and constructive feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Write a balanced appraisal: state what is good about a paper first, followed by criticisms; be polite and use a positive voice even when rating poorly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If possible, offer suggestions for improvement along with criticism. Polite and constructive feedback helps authors improve and reflects good reviewing practice.
